<a name="member-deleteIfExists-28-Path-29-"></a>

### `deleteIfExists(Path)`

```java
public static boolean deleteIfExists(Path path) throws IOException
```

Deletes a file, an empty directory or a symbolic link (never its
target) if it exists. Absence is the only failure this method reports
by returning; a non-empty directory, a denied permission or a parent
that is not a directory still fails.

**Parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | the entry to delete; borrowed for the call |

**Throws**

| Exception | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| [`DirectoryNotEmptyException`](DirectoryNotEmptyException.md) | if the entry is a non-empty directory |
| [`IOException`](../../io/IOException.md) | if the entry exists but cannot be deleted |

**Returns**

true if this call deleted the entry, false if it did not exist

<a name="member-createTempFile-28-Path-2c-String-2c-String-29-"></a>

### `createTempFile(Path,String,String)`

```java
public static Path createTempFile(Path dir, String prefix, String suffix) throws IOException
```

Creates a new empty file in `dir` and returns its path. The name
is the prefix, an unsigned decimal value from the host's secure random
source and the suffix; the file is created exclusively, with owner-only
read and write permission before the umask, and is never replaced. A
name that would contain a separator before its trailing separators is
rejected, as Java rejects a generated name with a parent.



Deleting the file stays the caller's responsibility: freeing the
returned path releases only the path object.

**Parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `dir` | an existing directory; borrowed for the call |
| `prefix` | the name's beginning, or null for none |
| `suffix` | the name's end, or null for `".tmp"` |

**Throws**

| Exception | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| [`IllegalArgumentException`](../../lang/IllegalArgumentException.md) | if the prefix or suffix would give the name a parent |
| [`InvalidPathException`](InvalidPathException.md) | if the prefix or suffix contains NUL |
| [`IOException`](../../io/IOException.md) | if the file cannot be created |

**Returns**

a fresh caller-owned path of the new file


[Back to member summary](#member-summary)

<a name="member-moveAtomicReplacing-28-Path-2c-Path-29-"></a>

### `moveAtomicReplacing(Path,Path)`

```java
public static Path moveAtomicReplacing(Path source, Path target) throws IOException
```

Renames `source` to `target` as one atomic file-system
operation, replacing an existing target: an observer sees either the
earlier target or the moved entry, never a missing or partial one. A
file may replace a file or link, and a directory an empty directory; a
link is renamed itself, and a target link is replaced, not followed. If
both names already denote the same file, nothing changes and both
remain. There is no copy fallback: a move across file systems fails
with [`AtomicMoveNotSupportedException`](AtomicMoveNotSupportedException.md), and every failure leaves
source and target unchanged. Atomic visibility is not a durability
guarantee after a crash.

**Parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `source` | the entry to move; borrowed for the call |
| `target` | its new name; borrowed for the call |

**Throws**

| Exception | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| [`AtomicMoveNotSupportedException`](AtomicMoveNotSupportedException.md) | if the names are on different file systems |
| [`IOException`](../../io/IOException.md) | if the rename fails, for example for a non-empty target directory or a missing source |

**Returns**

`target`, the caller's own path


[Back to member summary](#member-summary)

<a name="member-moveReplacing-28-Path-2c-Path-29-"></a>

### `moveReplacing(Path,Path)`

```java
public static Path moveReplacing(Path source, Path target) throws IOException
```

Moves `source` to `target`, replacing an existing target,
atomically when the host can rename. Only a regular file moved across
file systems, where no rename exists, is copied instead: into a new
exclusive temporary beside the target, with its mode and times, which
then replaces the target atomically before the source is removed. Any
failure before that replacement leaves the earlier target and the source
unchanged. If the source cannot be removed afterwards, the target
already holds the moved content and the method throws a
[`FileSystemException`](FileSystemException.md) whose reason is
`"Target replaced; source not removed"`; it does not roll the
target back. Other entries fail across file systems with
[`AtomicMoveNotSupportedException`](AtomicMoveNotSupportedException.md).

**Parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `source` | the entry to move; borrowed for the call |
| `target` | its new name; borrowed for the call |

**Throws**

| Exception | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| [`AtomicMoveNotSupportedException`](AtomicMoveNotSupportedException.md) | if a non-regular entry would cross file systems |
| [`IOException`](../../io/IOException.md) | if the move fails or its source remains after the replacement |

**Returns**

`target`, the caller's own path


[Back to member summary](#member-summary)

<a name="member-moveAtomicNoReplace-28-Path-2c-Path-29-"></a>

### `moveAtomicNoReplace(Path,Path)`

```java
public static Path moveAtomicNoReplace(Path source, Path target) throws IOException
```

Renames `source` to `target` only if no entry, not even a
dangling link, exists at the target, deciding that and renaming in one
atomic host operation, so a competing creator either wins and keeps its
entry or loses. Files and directories may move. The host primitive is
`renamex_np` with `RENAME_EXCL` on macOS and the
`renameat2` system call with `RENAME_NOREPLACE` on Linux;
where the kernel or file system lacks it, the call fails rather than
checking and renaming separately.

**Parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `source` | the entry to move; borrowed for the call |
| `target` | its new name, which must not exist; borrowed for the call |

**Throws**

| Exception | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| [`FileAlreadyExistsException`](FileAlreadyExistsException.md) | if the target exists, including when both names denote the same file |
| [`AtomicMoveNotSupportedException`](AtomicMoveNotSupportedException.md) | if the host or file system cannot rename exclusively, or the names are on different file systems |
| [`IOException`](../../io/IOException.md) | if the rename fails otherwise |

**Returns**

`target`, the caller's own path
